ai.literal: Murder - than those who undertake - is crueler indeed - harassment - having undertaken - unjust things - having done - behaving - king.
ai.translation: A king who rules by harassing his people and committing injustices is crueler than murderers.
ai.modern: மக்களைத் துன்புறுத்தி அநீதியான செயல்களைச் செய்து ஆட்சி நடத்தும் அரசன், கொலைத் தொழிலைச் செய்பவர்களை விடக் கொடியவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a tyrannical king to murderers, concluding that the king is far worse. The word 'கொலைமேற்கொண்டார்' refers to those who take up killing as their profession, such as assassins or robbers. The king is supposed to protect his people, but when he instead takes up 'அலை' (harassment or extortion) and does 'அல்லவை' (unjust deeds), his betrayal of duty makes him 'கொடிதே' (more cruel) than common murderers.

ai.literal: With a spear he who stood 'Give!' saying that is like, with a scepter he who stood begging.
ai.translation: A king holding a scepter who demands wealth from his subjects is like a highway robber standing with a spear and demanding, 'Give!'
ai.modern: ஆட்சி அதிகாரத்தைக் கையில் வைத்திருக்கும் அரசன் மக்களிடம் பொருளைக் கேட்பது, கையில் வேலுடன் வழியில் நிற்பவன் வழிப்போக்கர்களைப் பார்த்துப் பொருளைக் கொடு என்று மிரட்டிக் கேட்பதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a tyrannical king's taxation to highway robbery. The word 'kōl' refers to the king's scepter, a symbol of his power and duty to protect. When a king uses this power to demand wealth from his subjects, it is not a legitimate request. Instead, it is exactly like a bandit standing with a spear ('vēl') and ordering travelers to hand over their valuables. The imagery highlights the abuse of authority where protection turns into extortion.

ai.literal: Every day having examined justice who does not do king every day country will be ruined.
ai.translation: The country of a king who does not examine affairs and administer justice every day will fall into ruin day by day.
ai.modern: ஒவ்வொரு நாளும் குற்றங்களை ஆராய்ந்து நீதி வழங்காத அரசனது நாடு, நாளுக்கு நாள் அழிந்து போகும்.
ai.explanation: A king's primary duty is to actively oversee his administration and ensure justice is delivered continuously. If he fails to examine the daily affairs and correct wrongs, the foundation of his rule weakens. Consequently, his country will face steady and inevitable destruction day after day. The repetition of the word for 'every day' emphasizes that justice requires constant vigilance, not just occasional attention.

ai.literal: Wealth and subjects and together will lose, scepter having bent without considering acting king.
ai.translation: A king who acts without deliberation and bends his scepter will lose both his wealth and his subjects at once.
ai.modern: ஆராயாமல் செயல்பட்டு நீதியிலிருந்து தவறி ஆட்சி செய்யும் அரசு, தன் செல்வத்தையும் மக்களையும் ஒருசேர இழக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the dual consequences of unjust and thoughtless rule. The word 'கோல்' (scepter) represents justice, and its bending ('கோடி') signifies a deviation into tyranny. When a ruler acts without careful deliberation ('சூழாது'), they destroy the foundation of their own power, simultaneously losing both their material wealth ('கூழ்') and the loyalty of their citizens ('குடி').

ai.literal: suffering experienced unable to bear wept tears are they not wealth wearing away weapon
ai.translation: The tears wept by people unable to bear their suffering are the very weapon that will wear away the ruler's wealth.
ai.modern: துன்பப்பட்டு அதனைத் தாங்க முடியாமல் மக்கள் அழுத கண்ணீர்தான் ஆட்சியாளரின் செல்வத்தை அழிக்கும் ஆயுதமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns an unjust ruler about the destructive power of the people's sorrow. When subjects are oppressed and weep because they cannot bear their suffering, their tears are not merely signs of grief. The poet metaphorically equates these tears to a powerful weapon that will gradually wear away and destroy the king's wealth and prosperity. It emphasizes that a ruler's true security lies in the happiness of the people, not in military might or accumulated riches.

ai.literal: To kings, enduring is just rule; that if without, will not endure will become to kings glory.
ai.translation: A king's permanence lies in his just rule. Without it, his glory will not endure.
ai.modern: அரசர்களுக்கு நிலைத்து நிற்பது அவர்களின் செங்கோலாட்சியே ஆகும். அந்த நீதி தவறானால் அரசர்களின் புகழ் நிலைக்காமல் அழியும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet defines what makes a king's reign permanent. The word 'மன்னுதல்' means enduring or lasting forever, and the text states that only 'செங்கோன்மை' (a straight scepter, representing just rule) provides this permanence. The second half warns of the consequence of unjust rule. If justice is absent, the 'ஒளி' (light or glory) of the king will perish. Thus, a ruler's lasting fame and power depend entirely on their commitment to justice.

ai.literal: Drop absence to the world how, like that indeed king's grace absence living to beings.
ai.translation: Whatever the world suffers when there is not a drop of rain, living beings suffer the same when the king lacks grace.
ai.modern: மழைத்துளி இல்லாதபோது இந்த உலகம் எத்தகைய துன்பத்தை அடையுமோ, அதே போன்ற துன்பத்தை அரசனின் கருணை இல்லாதபோது வாழும் உயிர்கள் அடையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a direct parallel between the natural world and the political realm. It asks how the world fares without a single drop of rain, and answers that living beings fare exactly the same without the king's grace. The word 'அளி' can mean love, grace, or protection; here, in the context of unjust rule, it denotes the compassionate protection a just ruler owes their subjects. By comparing a cruel king to a severe drought, the text emphasizes that just rule is as essential to human survival as water is to the earth.

ai.literal: Than poverty it is painful, wealth, justice who-does-not-do king's scepter under if it falls.
ai.translation: If one falls under the scepter of a king who does not administer justice, possessing wealth is more painful than poverty.
ai.modern: நீதி வழங்காத அரசனது ஆட்சியின் கீழ் வாழ நேர்ந்தால், வறுமையை விடச் செல்வம் உடையவராக இருப்பதே ஒருவருக்கு அதிகத் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme insecurity of living under a tyrant. The phrase 'இன்மையின் இன்னாது உடைமை' states a paradox: having wealth is actually more painful than being in poverty. This happens when one's life falls under the scepter ('கோல்') of a king who does not govern justly ('முறைசெய்யா மன்னவன்'). Under such an unjust rule, a wealthy person becomes a constant target for extortion and confiscation, living in perpetual fear, whereas a poor person has nothing for the tyrant to steal.

ai.literal: Justice deviating, king if acts, raindrop deviating, will not happen sky raining.
ai.translation: If a king deviates from justice in his rule, the raindrops will deviate from their nature and the sky will fail to rain.
ai.modern: மன்னவன் நீதி முறை தவறி ஆட்சி செய்தால், மழைத்துளிகளும் தம் இயல்பிலிருந்து மாறி வானத்திலிருந்து பெய்யாமல் போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a direct parallel between the moral order of a kingdom and the natural order of the world. The word 'முறை' refers to justice, and 'கோடி' means bending or deviating. If a king bends the rules of justice in his governance, nature itself will deviate from its course. Consequently, the raindrops ('உறை') will fail, and the sky will refuse to pour down its showers, showing that unjust rule disrupts the very elements that sustain life.

ai.literal: Cow yield will diminish, those of six duties texts will forget, protector protects-not if.
ai.translation: If the protector fails to protect, the yield of cows will diminish and those of six duties will forget their texts.
ai.modern: நாட்டை ஆளும் அரசன் மக்களைக் காப்பாற்றாவிட்டால், பசுக்கள் பால் தருவது குறையும்; ஆறு தொழில்களை உடைய அறிஞர்கள் தங்கள் நூல்களை மறந்துவிடுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the breakdown of society when a ruler fails in his duty. The 'protector' (காவலன்) is the king, whose primary duty is to maintain order and justice. If he does not protect his people, the natural and social order collapses. The 'yield of cows' (ஆபயன்) diminishing represents the failure of nature and agriculture, while 'those of six duties' (அறுதொழிலோர்) forgetting their texts signifies the loss of learning, culture, and spiritual practices. Together, these images show that unjust rule destroys both material prosperity and intellectual life.
